A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title. All ten pages of each, including figures, tables, equations and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction results on InterHand2.6M, HIC and FreiHAND, component ablations in Table 4, and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative reconstructions reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same feature distillation and fusion, MANO regression, penetration-conditioned diffusion and collision-gradient guidance. Naming this the Foundation-to-Diffusion framework does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Training retains InterHand2.6M, Re:InterHand, COCO WholeBody, FreiHAND and HO-3D. Evaluation retains InterHand2.6M, HIC, FreiHAND and the same qualitative scenes; no dataset, task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each of Tables 1–3. The qualitative comparison also retains ACR and InterWild, despite its renumbering from Figure 3 to Figure 4.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the training settings, dataset counts, InterHand2.6M 5fps test protocol, alignment procedures and error metrics. The FreiHAND adaptation still omits relative translation estimation and two-hand diffusion.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same cumulative keypoint, segmentation, depth and diffusion ablations. The real-world case studies and their analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The reporting practice remains point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–4 match, including the Ours InterHand2.6M MRRPE/MPJPE/MPVPE values of 21.60/5.36/5.58 mm. The qualitative images, rankings and reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Feature-fusion equations (1)–(2), collision loss and guidance equations (3)–(4), and the collision criteria are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim efficient inference through distilled 2D priors, diffusion-based interaction refinement and state-of-the-art reconstruction across the same benchmarks. The new framework name and lightweight terminology restate these contributions without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explicit argument that generative priors require accurate initial alignment and reliable 2D cues to avoid implausible or unstable outputs, and emphasizes foundation-encoder computational costs. Experimental interpretations and the stated extreme-occlusion and motion-blur limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including ResNet-50, Sapiens, RTMDet, four A100 GPUs, AdamW, batch size 48 and the 1,000-step cosine diffusion schedule. Both versions retain the same promise of future code release without new access information.

R1.justification: The same 31 works are cited. However, the introduction shifts its diagnosis of existing methods from weakly constrained interaction priors toward a lack of dedicated alignment optimization, providing a limited revision of research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution list are substantially rewritten around the named Foundation-to-Diffusion framework and computational-efficiency narrative. Related work gains explicit single-hand/two-hand and 2D/generative-prior groupings. This revises the opening narrative substantially while retaining the technical sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced in size and its caption correctly changes rows to columns. V2 duplicates the identical pipeline diagram as Figures 2 and 3, renumbers the qualitative figure to Figure 4, and moves Table 4 from page 8 to page 9. These are presentation changes without new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the motivation and corrects Figure 1's caption, but duplicates the pipeline as Figures 2 and 3 on page 4, fragmenting the fusion-encoder explanation across pages 3–5. With the methods, empirical evidence and reproducibility information unchanged, this avoidable presentation defect outweighs the limited clarity gains and produces a small editorial decline.
